Subject: Marketplace listing copy alignment & support SLA matrix — preflight check

Hi Sam / Claire —

Pinging you both for a quick preflight before we submit the final listing assets for CloudBn (linked). We want to make sure the marketing copy and the support SLA table align with each marketplace's policy so this doesn't get held up in review. Key asks: 

- Can you confirm whether language like “enterprise-grade” or “bank-grade” is acceptable in the public listing, and if so what substantiation you expect?
- AWS/Azure both require a clear statement of support hours, response-time windows per severity level, and any regional differences — see attached `support_sla_matrix.xlsx`. Are the windows here sufficient?
- A couple of product claims we use: “<50ms inference latency (average)”, “99.9% production uptime for paid plans”, and “keeps customer data in-region when requested (VPC/on-prem options)”. Any red flags?

Attached: redwood_marketplace_copy_v3.docx (proposed listing copy), support_sla_matrix.xlsx, aws_listing_asset_pack.zip (logos, screenshots).

Internal: @Karthik — can you take a first pass on edits if the marketplaces flag anything? @Lauren — can legal quickly glance if there’s a stricter phrasing we should use for claims?

Thanks — want to lock this today if possible.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Torres <aws-marketplace-seller-ops@amazon.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing copy alignment & support SLA matrix — preflight check

Evelyn — thanks for the packet and the clear asks. Quick notes from the AWS Marketplace side (high level):

- "Enterprise-grade" is a marketing superlative we allow, but only if you can point to supporting artifacts on request (case studies, uptime history, SOC2). If you prefer to avoid extra review, safer phrasing: "production-ready" or "designed for enterprise workloads."
- For uptime claims, we need a single-number public SLA (e.g., 99.9%) tied to the offering. If you have tiered SLAs, provide explicit copy per tier. The spreadsheet looks OK but spell out whether the SLA is measured monthly or annually.
- Support: AWS requires hours-of-coverage, escalation path, and response-time commitments by severity. Your matrix lists response windows but please confirm whether those are initial response or resolution windows. AWS expects initial response times (e.g., Sev1: acknowledge within 1 hour, provide workaround within 4 hours) and then track to resolution separately.
- Latency statements should be phrased as typical/median or average with the test conditions documented; avoid absolute minimums. So: “typical inference latency of ~50 ms under x workload” is better than "<50ms".
- For data residency statements, include an explicit line that explains which features are in-region vs. not available in all regions (we often get escalations on mismatched expectations).

Attachments we’ll need to accept the listing: updated asset pack (logos + feature screenshots), a short one-page SLA PDF for the public page, and an internal technical contact for co-sell onboarding.

Please upload the one-pager and updated asset pack to the link you shared. I'll loop in the co-sell ops team after we have the final artifacts.

Thanks,
Sam Torres
AWS Marketplace — Seller Operations

Thanks Sam — useful checklist. Evelyn / Lauren, I pushed a couple of edits into `redwood_marketplace_copy_v3.docx` (see attached) and a cleaner public SLA one-pager: key changes summarized below: 

- Branding/claims: replaced "enterprise-grade" with "production-ready and validated in customer deployments"; moved specific latency numbers into a parenthetical with test conditions: "typical inference latency ~50 ms (measured on a 2xA100 instance with 512 token context)".
- SLA: public copy now states: "99.9% uptime for paid plans (monthly measurement)." In the private SLA we keep tiered language. The support matrix now clarifies "initial response" windows (Sev1: 1 hour acknowledge, Sev2: 4 hours, Sev3: next-business-day). Resolution targets remain internal / contractual.
- Escalation: added a short escalation ladder with contact roles and the commitment to provide an engineer response within 2 business hours for Sev1 after acknowledgement (we can soften if legal pushes back).

Attachments: updated `redwood_marketplace_copy_v4.docx` (attached), `support_sla_onepager.pdf`.

Lauren — can you do a quick pass for legal risk on the escalation wording and the phrase "validated in customer deployments"? If you flag anything, I can reword before we send the final pack.

—Karthik

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing copy alignment & support SLA matrix — preflight check

Thanks — Claire here from the Azure Marketplace validation team. Quick confirmation from our side:

- The suggested changes look good; we prefer "production-ready" over superlatives.
- Please remove any wording that reads as direct comparisons to platform providers (e.g., "works better than X's managed offering"). Platform-mention policies are strict.
- Azure requires the public listing to avoid detailed architectural claims that imply managed connectivity to Azure security services unless those integrations are certified — e.g., avoid stating "native Azure AD passthrough" unless you have a pointer to the integration doc.
- The one-pager SLA is acceptable; please include a single contact email for operational escalations (not a group alias) — this speeds approval.

I've attached `azure_marketable_copy_comments.pdf` with inline notes. Once you upload the revised asset pack and the single-point escalation contact, I can clear the listing for validation and share the marketplace listing URL for preview.

Claire Dupont
Azure Marketplace — Validation & Onboarding
